Sam (Support): Heads-up: Acme reports intermittent WS streams freezing for ~30-40s during idle periods on our Private VPC deployment. Works fine on hosted. Root cause suspected middlebox. Repro steps below, attaching logs when Lee uploads them.
Lee (acme): Yep. Using our edge appliance -> corporate NAT -> internet. Streams start fine, then after ~30s of silence the client gets a big chunk of buffered data and the connection stays open but app sees no events until buffered burst. Happens every 10-30m. No auth errors.
Taylor (SRE): Thanks. Two common culprits: (1) middlebox doing TCP/TLS idle buffering or (2) proxy injecting idle timeouts + silent RST/half-close. Does the appliance show any idle-timeout policy around 30s?
Lee (acme): Appliance config shows TCP idle close 60s, but we have a downstream firewall with TCP session timeout ~30s. Could be that one.
Priya (NetOps): If the firewall silently closes the flow or does NAT table coalescing you can see exactly this: server keeps sending small TLS records that get coalesced and released on teardown. Quick test: can you run a continuous small-payload ping from client -> server to keep bytes flowing? e.g., websocket-level pings every 15s.
Lee (acme): I can try adding a ws ping from the app. Any sample? We're Node-based.
Sam (Support): Paste this into your client startup to test (node ws lib):

```
const WebSocket = require('ws');
const ws = new WebSocket('wss://private.redwood.example');
ws.on('open', () => setInterval(() => ws.ping(), 15000));
```

Sam (Support): If ping keeps the stream alive that's a strong sign of idle-timeout/buffering. If it still stalls, then likely TLS record coalescing or proxy buffering on rewrite path.
Taylor (SRE): Also try forcing small TLS records to avoid coalescing: enable TCP_NODELAY and set write size small on client. On many clients you can disable Nagle: `socket.setNoDelay(true)`.
Priya (NetOps): Another angle: some middleboxes buffer until TLS close or application data boundary. Ask customer to capture a short pcap (client side) showing the quiet period — check if server is sending frames (TLS records) that aren't arriving to client until later.
Lee (acme): I captured one. Uploading now: `acme_ws_stall_2026-03-14.pcap` (link in DM). In the pcap we see server push segments at 00:00:34 but client only receives aggregated chunk at 00:01:08.
Taylor (SRE): That's exactly middlebox buffering. Two recommended paths:
- Short-term: enable websocket-level keepalive (ping) every 15s on clients and servers.
- Mid-term: ask network team to bump NAT/idle timeouts or exempt Redwood IPs from aggressive coalescing.
- Long-term: we could add an optional low-overhead keepalive frame from our side for Private deployments in customers with strict middleboxes.
Sam (Support): Can you confirm which IP ranges you're talking to? Priya: we should check if Private cluster egress IPs are on their allowlist and whether there are any DNAT/proxy hops that mutate TLS.
Priya (NetOps): Acme's firewall rules show an egress allowlist with stateful timeouts set low. Lee, if you can, please request a short window to set NAT timeout to 120s for 443 and test.
Lee (acme): Will do. Meanwhile I patched app with ping interval 12s and haven't seen a stall in 45m. Looks promising :thumbsup:
Taylor (SRE): Good. Please keep monitoring for 24h. Also Sam, can you create an internal ticket to consider runtime-level keepalive for Private clusters? Tag eng-runtime and product.
Sam (Support): Created ticket INF-6421, added logs and pcap link, assigned to @eng-runtime. deploy-bot: posted.
deploy-bot: Ticket INF-6421 created and assigned to eng-runtime.
Priya (NetOps): Action items summarized:
- Acme: temporarily increase NAT/session timeout to 120s and test.
- Acme: keep ws ping enabled in prod client for now.
- Redwood: consider optional server keepalive or doc note about middleboxes for Private customers.
Lee (acme): Thanks all. I'll update after firewall change.
Taylor (SRE): If Acme can't change firewall quickly we'll suggest a short patch in SDK to enable user-visible keepalive by default for Private endpoints.
Sam (Support): Closing loop later — leaving thread open for updates from Lee. :pray:
